units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: day 10
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a grey, damp day with outbreaks of drizzle and low cloud, lifting a little this afternoon. Hill and coastal fog patches clearing by midday. Southwesterly winds, light to moderate. Maximum temperature 10 C. Tonight: drizzle turning to showers, mild, minimum 8 C. Outlook: becoming unsettled, with pressure falling steadily through the week.

units.title: Inshore waters: Marrow Sound and approaches
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters forecast, valid 24 hours. Wind: southwest 3 or 4, occasionally 5 later. Sea state: slight or moderate. Weather: drizzle, showers later. Visibility: moderate or poor, occasionally very poor at first in the Lisle narrows, becoming good in showers.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver, day 10
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver harbour tides, day 10 (ST). High water 05:12 (4.1 m) and 17:38 (4.3 m). Low water 11:24 (0.9 m) and 23:51 (0.8 m). Neap tides. Sunrise 07:58, sunset 16:31.

units.title: Sound Lines service bulletin: day 10
units.author: ferry
units.text: 06:40. Due to low cloud and drizzle in the Lisle narrows, early sailings between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver may run up to 15 minutes late. All sailings are expected to operate. We apologise for any inconvenience.

units.author: ferry
units.text: 09:15. Visibility has improved and all Sound Lines services are now running to timetable. Customers are reminded that the saloon coffee machine on the Port Ammet to Lisle service is out of order. A replacement part has been ordered.

units.author: ferry
units.text: 15:00. Lisle pier: the seaward light at the end of the slipway is currently unreliable. Foot passengers boarding or leaving after dark should keep to the lit walkway and use the handrail. The council has been informed.

units.author: ferry
units.text: 20:30. Evening and night sailings are expected to operate, with possible delays of 5 to 15 minutes in drizzle. Passengers with bicycles must wait at the rail until directed by the deck crew.

units.title: Brackwater: supply fully restored
units.author: power
units.text: Restoration notice. Supplies to all customers in Brackwater and east Tollinby were restored by 02:14 following a fault at Brackwater substation. A damaged component has since been replaced and the site has returned to normal operation. Thank you for your patience. Claims guidance is available on request for outages exceeding 12 hours.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby Lane
units.author: power
units.text: Planned work notice. To allow pole replacement, supplies to properties on Tollinby Lane (numbers 2 to 48) and Orchard Close will be interrupted on day 11 between 09:00 and 13:00. Affected customers have been notified by letter. Please treat all equipment as live at all times.

units.title: Reporting a fault
units.author: power
units.text: Reminder. If you lose power, please check whether neighbours are also affected, then call the 24-hour fault line. Do not approach fallen lines; stay at least 10 metres away and report them immediately. Updates during outages are posted here and on local radio.

units.title: Recycling collections: Port Ammet
units.author: council
units.text: Some recycling collections in Port Ammet, including Rope Walk and Tanner Street, have been delayed due to staff shortages. Please leave bins out and they will be collected as soon as possible. We apologise for the disruption.

units.title: Brackwater junction: temporary signals
units.author: council
units.text: Temporary traffic signals remain in place at the Brackwater junction for carriageway and drainage works. Delays are possible at peak times. The works are scheduled to finish at the end of the month. Drivers are asked to follow signals and to avoid using the reservoir road as an alternative route, which is unsuitable for heavy traffic.

units.title: Water mains flushing: Gilliver
units.author: council
units.text: On behalf of the water company: mains flushing will take place in Gilliver on day 11 between 10:00 and 15:00. Customers may notice discoloured water or low pressure. Run the cold tap until clear. The water is safe to drink.

units.title: Notice to mariners 10/1: Lisle narrows
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. The south cardinal buoy marking the shoal in the Lisle narrows is reported unlit. Mariners are advised to navigate with caution and to keep a good lookout, particularly in reduced visibility. Repairs will be made when conditions allow.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners 10/2. Small-craft traffic to and from the landing stage on the north shore of Kittering Holm has increased while clearance works continue. Vessels in the area are asked to keep clear of the landing stage approach and to maintain a lookout for floating timber after strong winds.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: day 11
units.author: met
units.text: Today: cloudy with spells of light rain, becoming brighter with scattered showers this afternoon. Breezy, with southerly winds freshening. Very mild, maximum 11 C. Tonight: showers, some heavy in the west. Minimum 9 C. Outlook: a deepening area of low pressure is expected to approach from the southwest later in the week.

units.title: Inshore waters: Marrow Sound and approaches
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters forecast, valid 24 hours. Wind: south 4 or 5, increasing 6 at times later in the west. Sea state: moderate, occasionally rough later off Lisle's west coast. Weather: rain then showers. Visibility: good, occasionally moderate.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver, day 11
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver harbour tides, day 11 (ST). High water 05:55 (4.2 m) and 18:20 (4.4 m). Low water 12:06 (0.8 m). Sunrise 08:00, sunset 16:29. Moon: first quarter.

units.title: Sound Lines service bulletin: day 11
units.author: ferry
units.text: 06:40. All Sound Lines services are expected to run to timetable today. A reminder that the Lisle narrows south cardinal buoy is reported unlit; this does not affect scheduled sailings.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Passenger notice. Following a harbour notice under Byelaw 14, the slipways at Gilliver and Lisle are closed to pedestrians between sunset and sunrise. This does not affect ferry boarding, which takes place from the pier walkways. Please do not wait on or walk down the slipways after dark.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Winter timetable consultation. We are proposing to move the last weekday Gilliver sailing fifteen minutes earlier from next month to improve crew rest. Drop-in sessions will be held at Gilliver, Lisle and Port Ammet. Comments can also be left with terminal staff.

units.author: ferry
units.text: 20:30. Evening and night sailings are operating normally. Southerly winds may make the Gilliver approach lively after 22:00. Please remain seated during berthing.

units.author: power
units.text: Planned work complete. Supplies to Tollinby Lane and Orchard Close were restored at 12:20, ahead of schedule. Thank you to customers for their patience.

units.title: Precautionary inspections: coastal substations
units.author: power
units.text: Following the Brackwater fault, we are carrying out precautionary inspections of older transformer components at coastal substations, including Gilliver and Port Ammet North. Inspections are not expected to interrupt supplies. Where short planned interruptions are needed, customers will be notified in advance.

units.title: Gilliver: brief interruption
units.author: power
units.text: Fault notice. A brief interruption affected around 200 customers in Gilliver between 14:10 and 14:38 while a protective device was reset during inspection work. All supplies have been restored. We apologise for any inconvenience.

units.author: council
units.text: Update on recycling collections. Agency drivers will provide cover for the affected round from Monday. Glass collections in Tollinby will resume within the next fortnight. Residents whose bins have been missed may report them online and we will arrange a return visit.

units.title: Lisle pier lighting repair
units.author: council
units.text: Our electrical contractor will attend Lisle pier on Friday to repair the seaward light at the end of the slipway. Work will take place at low water and the slipway will be closed while it is carried out. Pier walkways will remain open.

units.title: Planning notices: check the portal
units.author: council
units.text: Residents are reminded that genuine planning notices and decisions are published on the council's planning portal and on site. Images shared online that differ from the portal should not be relied on. If you are unsure whether a notice is genuine, please contact the planning office.

units.title: Notice to mariners 11/1
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. The south cardinal buoy in the Lisle narrows has been relit and is operating normally. Notice 10/1 is cancelled.

units.author: coast
units.text: Advance notice. Owners of small craft moored in Gilliver, Lisle and Port Ammet are advised that strong winds are likely later in the week. Check moorings, remove loose gear and outboard engines from tenders, and make arrangements to haul out where possible.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: day 12
units.author: met
units.text: Today: sunny spells and scattered showers, with good visibility between them. Southerly winds, fresh to strong on exposed coasts. Maximum 12 C, unusually mild. Tonight: showers merging into longer spells of rain. Outlook: a deep low will cross the region late on day 13 and through day 14, bringing gales, heavy rain and large waves.

units.title: Yellow warning: wind and rain, days 13 to 14
units.author: met
units.text: Yellow warning of wind and rain, valid from 18:00 on day 13 until 15:00 on day 14. Southerly gales, with gusts of 55 to 65 mph widely and up to 70 mph on exposed headlands and islands. 30 to 50 mm of rain possible. Expect disruption to ferries, power cuts, and damage to trees and temporary structures.

units.title: Inshore waters: Marrow Sound and approaches
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters forecast, valid 24 hours. Wind: south 5 to 7, increasing gale 8 later in the west. Sea state: moderate or rough, becoming very rough later off Lisle and Kittering Holm. Weather: showers, rain later. Visibility: good, becoming moderate or poor.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver, day 12
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver harbour tides, day 12 (ST). High water 06:41 (4.4 m) and 19:03 (4.6 m). Low water 00:31 (0.7 m) and 12:52 (0.6 m). Note: a southerly surge may raise water levels above predicted heights on days 13 and 14. Sunrise 08:02, sunset 16:27.

units.title: Sound Lines service bulletin: day 12
units.author: ferry
units.text: 06:40. All services today are expected to run, with some movement on the Lisle crossing in a fresh southerly. Please note the Met Office warning for days 13 and 14. Night sailings on day 13 and sailings on day 14 are at risk of cancellation. Decisions will be posted here by 15:00 on day 13.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Freight customers. Space on day 12 and morning day 13 sailings is limited due to increased bookings ahead of the forecast weather. Please contact the freight desk before travelling. Unsecured loads will not be accepted.

units.author: ferry
units.text: 20:30. Night sailings are operating, with possible delays on the Gilliver approach due to swell. The Gilliver slipway chain is in place from sunset; foot passengers should use the pier walkway.

units.title: Storm readiness
units.author: power
units.text: Ahead of the forecast gale, we have additional crews on standby across the region. Power cuts are possible, particularly in exposed coastal areas. Please charge phones and torches, keep the fault line number to hand, and check on vulnerable neighbours. Never approach a fallen line.

units.author: power
units.text: Customers using medical equipment that depends on electricity should make sure they are on our priority services register. Generators must never be run indoors or connected directly to household wiring.

units.author: power
units.text: Inspection update. Precautionary checks at Gilliver and Port Ammet North substations are complete. No defects requiring immediate action were found. Further inspections at smaller sites will continue after the forecast weather has passed.

units.author: council
units.text: Brackwater junction: the junction is temporarily closed following an incident within the roadworks. Diversions are signed via Tollinby. We will update this notice when the road reopens. Please do not use the reservoir road as a through route.

units.author: council
units.text: Update 17:35. The Brackwater junction has reopened in both directions. Temporary signals remain in operation. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Preparing for the gale
units.author: council
units.text: With strong winds forecast on days 13 and 14, please bring in or secure wheelie bins, garden furniture and trampolines. Collections on day 14 may be suspended if conditions are unsafe. Port Ammet sports hall will be available as a rest centre if needed. Sandbags are available from the depot at Tanner Street while stocks last.

units.title: Navigational warning: gale
units.author: coast
units.text: Gale warning issued for the Marrow Sound and approaches, valid from day 13 evening. Small craft should remain in harbour. Vessels making passage near Kittering Holm and Lisle's west coast should expect very rough seas and floating debris, including timber.

units.author: coast
units.text: The public are asked to stay away from harbour walls, breakwaters and slipways during the gale. Waves may overtop walls without warning. In an emergency at sea or on the coast, call the emergency number and ask for the Coastguard.

units.title: LB-0031: Brackwater reservoir dam works, 1976 (A. Treloar reel)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no.: LB-0031. Date: summer 1976 (from box label). Location: Brackwater reservoir, dam works compound. Kit: quarter-inch open reel, 7.5 ips, mono, single dynamic microphone. Duration: 31 min 40 s. Description: pile driving and machinery during dam strengthening works; site voices; a lorry reversing; skylarks. Condition: moderate print-through (pre- and post-echo) on loud transients. Digitised by N. Ashby.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0031, continued. Section 3 (21:10 to 31:40): recorded after works ceased for the day, per the recordist's spoken note. Wind and water over the spillway. At 24:05, 26:50 and 29:12, percussive events, unattributed, four to five strikes each at regular intervals. The pile driver is not running in this section according to the recordist's note. Curator's note: attribution left open.

units.title: LB-0044: Dawn chorus, Brackwater car park, 1988
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no.: LB-0044. Date: spring 1988. Location: Brackwater estate car park, east edge. Kit: cassette walkman, built-in microphone. Duration: 44 min. Description: dawn chorus, robin, wren, blackbird, wood pigeon, a distant tractor. Recordist coughs at 03:11. Condition: tape hiss, wow on the first two minutes. Provenance: donated by the recordist's daughter.

units.title: LB-0012: Gilliver foghorn, 1971 (uncertain)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no.: LB-0012. Date: given as 1971 on the box; the recordist's handwriting may read 1977. Location: Gilliver harbour wall. Kit unknown. Duration: 6 min 20 s. Description: foghorn at roughly 30 s intervals, gulls, a diesel engine idling, a man saying 'that'll do'. Curator's note: Gilliver had no foghorn after 1969 according to the harbour office; provenance under review.

units.title: Window lamp (Gilliver custom)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The window lamp is a household custom recorded in Gilliver and, less often, in Lisle, in which a lamp or candle is kept lit in a front window facing the water through the night. It is described by those who keep it as 'manners' or a courtesy, and is said to let 'them' know 'the house is awake'. It is recorded since at least the 1880s [parish notes, Society holdings].

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Practice. Lamps were traditionally oil, later electric. The lamp is lit at dusk and left until daylight, and is not put out for visitors. Accounts differ on whom the lamp is for: returning boats, travellers on the shore road, or the dead [Gilliver Oral History Project, 1976]. The custom declined after the 1960s and has been observed by fewer households since [citation needed].

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: 'since at least the 1880s'. This claim is poorly sourced. The parish note cited mentions 'a light kept in the window at the Rendles' in 1886, which is one household and could as easily be a sickroom lamp. I would amend to 'recorded in one household in 1886 and widely from the 20th century'. The 'them' in the lead is the oral history's word; it should be in quotation marks or removed.

units.title: Holm timber camp ledger, Nov. 1894 (J. Penhallow)
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 12th. Wind S.W., wet. Men at work 21. Felled on the south lines 64, of which 9 spoilt in the fall. Hauled to the shore 40. Wages paid Saturday last in full, 18s. the man, Trebilcock & sons 22s. for the horse. Bought of the Gilliver boat: flour 2 sacks, bacon, lamp oil 4 gall., tobacco. Rain all the afternoon, the men in early.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 14th. Fair, cold. Men at work 21. Felled 71, a good tally. Discharged Jas. Moyle for drink and sent him off by the boat, he cursing the Holm and all upon it. A sharp frost after dark, the first. The men keep the lamps burning in the long hut all night, which is a great waste of oil, but I have not the heart to forbid it.

units.title: Carrow Point light, keeper's log, Nov. 1907 (E. Strake)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Nov. 3rd. Middle watch, E. Strake. 0000 wind S.W. 4, vis. good, lamp burning well, clockwork wound. 0130 rain. 0200 vis. moderate. 0300 steamer passed westward, lights seen. 0400 relieved by assistant keeper. Remarks: none. Oil used 2 pints. Brass done. Fog signal not required.

units.title: Field notebook: islands of the Sound, 1923 (H. Arnell)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Kittering Holm, first day. Landed 10 a.m. by Mr Penrose's boat. North shore: oystercatchers (12), turnstones, a pair of herons at the old curing station wall. Woodland: coal tit, goldcrest in numbers, treecreeper, wren. Bracken dense. [Sketch of a fern frond, labelled Dryopteris sound-form?] Mr Penrose declined my offer of tea and insisted on fetching me at four, 'not a minute after'. Boatmen are a superstitious tribe.

units.title: Diary of Amos Rendle, Gilliver, 1934
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mon. Blowing S. Did not go out. Mended pots in the shed with Father. Crab at 4d the lb at Ammet, which is robbery. Walked past the old curing station on the way back from the Holm side last week and the roof is all in now. I was a boy there carrying salt. Never a sick man was sent there whatever they say in the Ammet bars, only fish.

units.title: From the 1894 files: the Holm camp's supply boat
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. From the Courier of November 1894, page 6, the weekly 'Gilliver Notes'. The paper's village correspondent wrote these columns anonymously for nearly twenty years. This item records the timber camp on Kittering Holm in its first season. The figures for the men's wages are as printed; we have not been able to check them against any other source.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The Holm continues to resound with the axe, and our harbour has not been so busy since the herring years. Mr Penrose's boat goes across thrice weekly laden with flour, oil and other necessaries, and returns with tales of great trees laid low. The men, it is said, earn a handsome eighteen shillings, and the village publicans are already counting the coming spring.

units.title: Kittering Holm fish-curing station
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The Kittering Holm fish-curing station was a herring salting and smoking works on the north shore of the Holm, operating seasonally from about 1882 until the early 1910s [lease, Society holdings]. Herring landed at Gilliver were ferried across, gutted and packed by local women and girls, and returned for sale on the mainland. The ruined seaward wall survives.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The 'quarantine station'. The station is sometimes described as a quarantine station. There is no record of any medical or quarantine use. The claim appears to originate in a newspaper rumour in the early 20th century, which was corrected [Courier, back issues; citation needed for exact date]. Workers interviewed in 1976 recalled only fish, smoke and cold.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: closure date. 'Until the early 1910s' is fair. I would add the obvious context that every curing station on the Sound closed within the same two decades as the herring moved and rail freight changed the trade. Nothing about the Holm station's closure needs explaining beyond that. I note the article does not say this and the omission invites mischief.

units.title: Kittering Holm timber camp (1894-95)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: A timber camp operated on Kittering Holm during the winter of 1894-95, felling softwood for pit props and fencing. At its height it employed 21 men and a horse team, housed in a long hut near the landing. The camp ended in midwinter, earlier than planned, and the men returned to Gilliver. Its clerk's ledger survives and has been transcribed [Society holdings]. The reason for the early end is disputed (see talk).

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project, 1976: tape 4 (the lamp)
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Your mother kept a lamp in the window? Mrs E.P., aged 84: Every night of her life. Every night. Interviewer: What was it for? Mrs E.P.: For the boats, so they could see the houses coming in. [pause] Well, that's what she said. My father said it was for the men on the shore road. Interviewer: Which men? Mrs E.P.: I couldn't tell you. He didn't say. [laughs] They didn't, did they.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Do you keep one? Mrs E.P.: Oh yes. Electric now, my son put it in. Interviewer: Have you ever let it go out? Mrs E.P.: Once, in the war, for the blackout. We had to. [long pause] My mother sat up all night by the window instead. She said it was only manners. Interviewer: Manners to whom? Mrs E.P.: Well. To whoever was passing.

units.title: Holm timber camp ledger, Nov. 1894, contd.
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 19th. Wind N., hard frost. Men at work 20. Felled 58. The ground like iron on the north lines, the saws binding. Bought of the boat: lamp oil 6 gall., the most yet, and candles. Hoskins complains of a cough. Read the 121st psalm to the men at supper at their asking, they being low after a man went missing an hour on the far line and came in very quiet.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 21st. Fair. Men at work 20. Felled 66. Wages: 18s. the man, paid in coin from the box, all accounted. Pellow asks that the far lines be worked first in the day and the near lines last, so the men come in toward the hut as the light goes. I have agreed it, the order of work being much the same to the tally.

units.title: Carrow Point light, keeper's log, Nov. 1907, contd.
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Nov. 9th. Middle watch, E. Strake. 0000 wind N.W. 3, vis. very good, stars. Lamp burning well. 0115 fishing boats returning to Gilliver, three lights. 0230 frost on the gallery rail. 0400 relieved. Remarks: shore road lamp at Carrow farm gate out again; reported to the farmer in the morning. Oil used 2 pints.

units.title: Field notebook, 1923, contd.
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Holm, second day. Interior. Excellent browse throughout: bramble, ivy, young holly, all unbrowsed, which surprised me. Woodcock flushed twice. A badger sett, apparently disused, near the ridge. Fungi abundant [list follows]. I would have expected roe at least on an island this size with this cover. None seen. Mr Penrose again refused to land at the north shore in the afternoon, and fetched me from the stage at a quarter to four.

units.title: Diary of Amos Rendle, 1934, contd.
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Weds. Fair at last. Out at 5 with Father, hauled the Holm side string, 30 pots, good brown crab and two lobster. Lost a net at the rocks under the old station, caught fast, had to cut it. Father would not go back in for it with the light going. Mother had the lamp lit when we came in. Paid 3s. for new twine.

units.title: From the 1890s files: the herring girls
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. Another 'Gilliver Notes' column, from the autumn of 1896. It describes the fish-curing station on the Holm at the height of its season, and is one of very few contemporary descriptions of the work. Readers will notice the correspondent's fondness for adjectives. We print it unaltered.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The herring are in, and so are the girls of Gilliver, who cross daily to the curing station on the Holm with their knives and their songs. One may smell the smoke-houses from the church porch when the wind is in the east. The work is hard and cold, the pay a fair one, and the girls return each evening on the last boat before dusk, as their mothers insist they must.

units.title: LB-0058: Gilliver harbour at night, 1993
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no.: LB-0058. Date: winter 1993. Location: Gilliver harbour wall, by the slipway. Kit: DAT portable, stereo pair. Duration: 58 min. Description: halyards, a moored boat's generator, rain showers, a dog barking on the hill, a door closing at 22:40. Curator's note: recordist notes 'lamps in most windows on the front' in the box insert. No incidents logged.

units.title: Holm timber camp ledger, Nov.-Dec. 1894
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 28th. Wind E., bitter. Men at work 18, Hoskins sick in the hut, Jno. Pascoe gone home by the boat at his own asking, wages paid him to the day. Felled 47. Hoskins & Pellow would not go to the far line after the lamps were lit, tho' it was but half past four and light enough to see. Docked them a quarter day. They took it without complaint, which I like less than if they had complained.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 2nd. Sabbath. No work. Snow in the night, a light fall. Walked the near lines with Trebilcock after service to see the tally marks. Tracks in the snow along the far line, which T. says are the men's, from Saturday. I said there was no snow Saturday. He said then they are from this morning. No man went out this morning. Let it be.

units.title: Carrow Point light, keeper's log, Nov. 1907, contd.
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Nov. 15th. Middle watch, E. Strake. 0000 wind calm, vis. good, slight mist low on the water. Lamp burning well. 0240 Remarks: two persons on the shore road below the light, walking toward Carrow farm, no lantern. Hailed from the gallery. Did not answer. Not seen to pass the farm gate. 0400 relieved. Oil used 2 pints.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Nov. 16th. Morning watch, assistant keeper's hand. 0400 wind S. 2, vis. good. 0600 lamp extinguished at sunrise, curtains drawn. Remarks: P.K. asked whether I saw anyone on the road in the night. I did not. Carrow farmer says none of his were out. Brass done. Supply boat Thursday.

units.title: Field notebook, 1923, contd.
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Holm, third day. Searched the ridge and the soft ground by the burn for slots and droppings. No slots of deer. No droppings. No fraying on the saplings, no lying-up places in the bracken, no paths but my own. A wren's nest, very late. I shall widen the search tomorrow. Mr Penrose asked me whether I had seen anything, and when I said no deer, he seemed relieved, which is a curious thing for a boatman to be.

units.title: Diary of Amos Rendle, 1934, contd.
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Fri. Gale from the S. all day, boats in. Helped haul the Pascoes' boat up the slip with the whole street on the rope. Lights went out in the village at 9 when the line blew down at the hill. Every house lit a lamp in the front window, Mother first. Father sat up. Wind dropped by 3. Nobody's boat lost, thank God.

units.title: From the 1911 files: the 'quarantine' rumour
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. Readers have asked where the idea of a 'quarantine station' on Kittering Holm came from. As far as we can tell, it came from us. The column below, from the spring of 1911, repeats a rumour heard in Ammet. We print it in full because the history society has asked for it. A correction appeared the following week; we will print that too.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: There is talk in the Ammet bars, which your correspondent passes on without endorsing, that the old curing station upon the Holm is to be made a quarantine station for sailors brought in sick from foreign ports. Gilliver is not pleased by the notion. It is said by some that the place was once so used in the cholera years, though no one can name the year, nor the sailor.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: why the camp ended. The article implies something unexplained. The simpler reading is a pay dispute. The ledger shows docked wages from late November, men leaving 'at their own asking', and a clerk who complains the men 'took it without complaint', which is how men behave when they have already decided to go. Camps broke up over pay all the time. I propose a sentence to that effect.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Talk, reply. A pay dispute is plausible and I have no objection to it being mentioned as one view. But the ledger also records wages 'paid in coin from the box, all accounted' as late as 21 November, and the clerk's own entries concern lamps and the order of work rather than money. I would prefer the article to say 'the reason is disputed' and leave both readings on this page.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project, 1976: tape 7 (the lamp, again)
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: People have told us the lamp was for the boats. Mr J.T., aged 79: No. No, the harbour has its own light for that. The lamp's for them on the road. Interviewer: Who is on the road? Mr J.T.: Folk walking. Interviewer: At night? Mr J.T.: [pause] You keep the lamp lit, they know you're awake, they walk on. That's all it is. My wife thinks it's for her mother. Let her.

units.title: LB-0063: Brackwater reservoir edge, night, 1997
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no.: LB-0063. Date: autumn 1997. Location: Brackwater reservoir, west footpath near the outflow. Kit: DAT portable, stereo omnis. Duration: 72 min. Description: tawny owls, water over the outflow weir, a vehicle on the reservoir road at 00:40. Percussive events, unattributed, at 01:12 and 01:55. Recordist's note on the insert: 'booster pump?' with a question mark.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0063, provenance. Donated by the recordist, a former water company employee, with a note that the booster pump 'ran at night in those days as well'. No pump log for 1997 survives. Curator's note: the pump explanation is the recordist's own and is recorded here as such.

units.title: Carrow Point lighthouse
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Carrow Point lighthouse stands on the headland north of Port Ammet and has shown a white flashing light since its completion in the 1850s. It was staffed by a principal keeper and an assistant until automation forty years ago. The keepers' logbooks for several decades survive in the Society's holdings, partly transcribed by volunteers.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Logbooks. The logs record wind, visibility, lamp checks and passing vessels at regular intervals through each watch. A 'remarks' column was used for anything else. Remarks in the early 1900s include repairs, visitors, wildlife and, on several nights, people seen on the shore road below the light who did not answer when hailed [Strake logs, transcription in progress]. These were not reported further.
